content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices during sharp upward moves, then fails to correct downward after peaks.
- Shows persistent lag in responding to recent price declines — forecasts remain too high longer than warranted.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured; model holds onto high forecasts too long after a peak.
- Tends to overcorrect downward after a spike, leading to premature troughs that don’t align with true market behavior.
- Underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture sudden reversals or sharp directional shifts in the last 7–10 days.
- When history shows a strong downward trend, model often fails to recognize the continuation and underestimates the depth of the drop.
